column2: The 19 distinct enzyme PAIRS of the iMARS fusion set.
iMARS reports 36 fusion constructs, but a construct is a linker variant:
fifteen of the 36 are 4CL-STS with different linkers. ChannelBridge does
not fuse anything -- it searches for a relative POSE that a bispecific
binder could hold -- so the linker is not a variable here and the unit of
an example is the pair. Collapsing the 36 on (upstream, downstream) gives
these 19, numbered by first appearance in the paper's construct table.
upstream/downstream matters and is not cosmetic: O_IC is measured at the
UPSTREAM exit only, so swapping the two changes the score.

column4: That is GENE order, which is not the same as the metabolic order
in the two columns before it -- iMARS_01 is 4CL upstream of STS
and most of its constructs put STS first in the chain. Not a
contradiction: which end of the fusion an enzyme sits at says
nothing about which direction the intermediate travels.

column3: which tunnel source each side STARTS from, per enzymes.tsv.

column4: mixed means one enzyme of the pair is annotated in ChannelsDB
and the other is not, so one tunnel is fetched and the other
computed inside a single pair file.
It is not where the tunnel ends up coming from. A fetched chain
that stops before the surface is handed to CAVER instead, seeded
from the site the database identified, so most "channelsdb"
sides here actually resolve to a seeded CAVER run. The `resolved`
column of report.tsv records what really produced each tunnel,
and `recovery` whether the seeded run found the annotated route.
